subject: Sealed-tunnel handoff & control/data separation checklist for Glassworks private deployment
messages:
From: Ali Khan <ali.khan@glassworks.net>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@glassworks.net, solutions@edgebridge.io
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning handoff for private deploy — questions on demarcation

Hi Vivek / team,

Thanks for the call today. A couple of items we want captured before the runbook is finalized:

- We plan to terminate the sealed WireGuard tunnel on our perimeter router (ASA-4k). Is Redwood expecting the tunnel to land on a single IP or a small announced /30?
- Control plane calls (model management, metrics, heartbeats) need to traverse the sealed tunnel but must be logically separated from data-plane inference traffic which will egress directly to our NAT pool. We'd like your acceptance criteria for that separation.
- Cert rotation: what's the recommended TTL and automation approach for the control-plane client certs?
- MTU and path-MTU suggestions — our infra prefers 1400 for GRE/VXLAN but you're likely to have different needs for large tokens.

Attaching a sketch we drew — sealed_tunnel_handshake_diagram.pdf. Can you confirm who owns the BFD/hold-time negotiation, and whether Redwood will set up observability endpoints for connection health?

Goal: finalize the "handoff-checklist.xlsx" and sign off on the demarc responsibilities by next Tue (2026-09-14).

Best,
Ali
Senior Cloud Architect
Glassworks

Attachment: sealed_tunnel_handshake_diagram.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ali Khan <ali.khan@glassworks.net>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, EdgeBridge Integrations <solutions@edgebridge.io>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sealed-tunnel handoff & control/data separation checklist for Glassworks private deployment

Ali — thanks for the clear sketch. I pulled together a concise acceptance checklist and a set of operational defaults so we can converge quickly. Please see inline answers and next steps below.

1) Tunnel termination addressing
- Preferred: single anycast VIP per region (customer announces a /32 to their perimeter) or a dedicated /30 if you need a physical point-to-point for HA. Either works; operationally we prefer a small announced range so we can float endpoints during maintenance.
- Action: Glassworks to confirm choice in the checklist (column: IP plan).

2) Control plane vs data plane separation (acceptance criteria)
- Control plane (CP): all management/metrics/rollout API calls MUST traverse the sealed tunnel and terminate on the control-plane gateway. CP flows are authenticated with mTLS client certs and are restricted to ports 443 and 8443.
- Data plane (DP): inference data (LLM tokens/payloads) will be delivered to the local inference fabric and may egress via your NAT pool for external model shards or telemetry, depending on policy. DP must NOT use the CP certificate chain.
- Acceptance checks: CP traffic observable on our tracer endpoint, no DP flows observed on CP ports during a 10-minute capture, and model-serving metrics present on the CP telemetry stream.

3) Cert rotation
- We recommend automated rotation every 30 days with 5-day overlap (new cert introduced before expiry). Redwood supports ACME-style rotation via a signed CSR workflow or can accept pre-provisioned certs pushed to the control-plane PKI.
- Action: indicate preferred automation option in spreadsheet.

4) MTU
- Practical suggestion: 1400 for encapsulated paths to be conservative. If you can guarantee jumbo frames across the path, we can support 1500+ for large-batch inference. We'll include an MTU probe step in the cutover.

5) BFD/hold-time and observability
- BFD: default timers we propose are 300ms detect, 100ms interval (aggressive) for low-latency detection. If Glassworks wants more conservative timers, we'll accept 1s detect.
- Observability: Redwood will export a health endpoint for the CP gateway (Prometheus-style /metrics + a short JSON status ping). We'll also configure a fallback webhook to your NetOps on state changes.

Attachments: I attached a draft handoff-checklist.xlsx that maps responsibilities (Redwood vs Glassworks) and includes verification scripts. Jonas and Kimberly — please review the acceptance tests and add operational playbooks where needed.

Next steps / timeline:
- Glassworks: fill IP plan + cert automation preference (by Mon EOD).
- Redwood: produce final runbook and smoke-test scripts (by Tue morning).
- Cutover window tentatively Wed 09/15 01:00–04:00 UTC.

I'll follow up with a short runbook snippet in the thread.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sealed-tunnel handoff & control/data separation checklist for Glassworks private deployment

Adding ops acceptance details and a short rollback plan. Quick items to call out from an SRE perspective:

- Preflight smoke tests (Redwood):
  * TLS handshake validation (client cert chain validation script)
  * Control-plane API list: /models, /rollouts, /health — each must return 200 within 500ms for baseline acceptance
  * Telemetry ingestion: confirm control-plane metrics appear in our Grafana datasource (test ID: GLW-CP-TEST).

- Glassworks prechecks:
  * Routing: ensure AS path for announced VIP is present in BGP table and not filtered by RPKI policies.
  * Firewall: allow outbound 443/8443 from CP gateway to Redwood egress ranges.

- Rollback plan (if CP handshake fails at cutover):
  1) Revert BGP announcement to previous route via your route reflector (Glassworks ops).
  2) Disable sealed tunnel on Glassworks ASA and switch to maintenance stub (EdgeBridge will assist).
  3) Point traffic to passive CP endpoint while we diagnose (Jonas/Redwood).

- Security notes:
  * All CP audit logs will be forwarded to your SIEM over TLS; we will also provide signed evidence of what certs were used during the handshake window for compliance.

I updated the handoff-checklist.xlsx with the smoke-test commands and short Jira tasks. Jonas — I'll need the canary endpoint and an ops contact for the night window.

Kimberly
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligned with what we expected. Quick confirmations from our side:

- We'll announce a /30 for the initial pilot (we can move to a VIP later). IPs will be listed in the spreadsheet by EOD.
- Cert automation: we'll use the pre-provisioned PKI option and push certs via your CSR endpoint.
- MTU: we'll set path MTU probes to 1400 by default for the pilot.
- BFD: we'll accept the 1s detect timers for the pilot window.

I'll fill the spreadsheet and ping here when done (aiming for today so we can keep the Wed window). Appreciate the thorough rollback plan — we'll loop our on-call for the cutover.

Regards,
Ali
